title: Surface Area and Volume of Prisms
seo_title: Grade 8 Surface Area and Volume Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 8: 4.2 Surface area and volume of 3D objects
standard_text: Use appropriate formulae to calculate the surface area, volume and capacity of cubes, rectangular prisms and triangular prisms; describe the interrelationship between surface area and volume of the objects mentioned above; use and convert between appropriate SI units.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 surface area and volume worksheets: rectangular and triangular prisms, capacity and missing lengths. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Surface area: add all the faces.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Volume of a prism = area of the cross-section × length.
  • Triangular prism: V = ½ × b × h × l.
  • Surface area = the total area of all the faces (use a net).
  • 1 cm³ = 1 mℓ, 1 000 cm³ = 1 ℓ, 1 m³ = 1 000 ℓ.

Examples

Example

A triangular prism: triangle base 6 cm, height 4 cm, length 10 cm

½ × 6 × 4 = 12 cm²

Answer: V = 120 cm³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The slant edgeUse the perpendicular height.
Some faces onlyAdd every face.
100 for cubic units1 cm³ = 1 000 mm³.
